tasks.short: Direct helpers placing crane blocking or outrigging

steps.what: Direct helpers placing blocking or outrigging under cranes and observe their actual placement

tasks.design: Keep live direction and observation with the operator, supported by existing setup guidance in {DOCS}. No generated instruction or recorded completion flag replaces observing the helpers' actual work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Setup depends on actual equipment and site conditions while helpers perform physical work.
tasks.enabler_now: Reference guidance supports the operator but does not direct helpers safely by itself.
tasks.still_hard: Communicate clearly and recognise when placement or conditions require stopping and clarification.
tasks.human_edge: Observe the actual setup and coordinate people in real time.
tasks.altitude: Direction and setup responsibilities remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Use clear communication and recognise unresolved setup concerns.

evidence.claim: Directing crane setup helpers is live coordination of physical work, not warehouse record keeping.

assumptions: Boundary is operator direction and observation, excluding the helpers' physical placement and separate engineering or lift-planning work.

Existing responsible personnel supply the setup requirements before s1. The operator observes current site conditions and helper actions during retained s1 time; helper actions occur after directions within the ongoing exchange, not as a pre-existing completion input.
Helper labour remains unchanged outside the focal denominator. No free structured setup-ready flag is assumed.
Native guidance access suffices. No new device, application, capture obligation or upkeep is introduced, so incremental work is zero.
unknowns: Crane type and current setup responsibilities
research_questions: Which setup concerns most often require clarification between operators and helpers?

already_counted.description: All live direction and observation remains.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. No coordination or physical observation is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Determine load weights and check lifting capacity

steps.what: Determine load weights and verify the actual load and lifting configuration
Check load weights against applicable lifting capacities and resolve uncertain comparisons

tasks.design: Keep weight verification and capacity checking with the operator using current equipment information in {DOCS}. Existing installed indicators remain part of the present equipment; no new calculation service or automatic permission to lift is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: A numeric comparison is only useful when load and configuration information are correct.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing capacity information supports the check without removing verification work.
tasks.still_hard: Identify uncertain weights and ensure that the capacity information applies to the actual configuration.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise an unsupported assumption and seek clarification rather than treating a number as clearance.
tasks.altitude: Weight and capacity-checking responsibilities remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Distinguish verified load facts from estimates and configuration assumptions.

evidence.claim: Load and configuration verification is necessary contextual work; existing indicator arithmetic cannot be counted again as a new labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary is determining weights and comparing with capacity, excluding lift planning, crane control and engineering approval.

Existing load owners provide load information and the equipment owner provides current capacity documentation before the task. The operator verifies actual load identity, weight basis and crane configuration during s1; no free structured verified-weight or safe-to-lift flag is assumed.

The operator chooses applicable capacity information and resolves uncertainty during retained s2 time. Missing or conflicting facts follow the existing manual clarification route, with no inferred values.
Native equipment information and existing indicators remain unchanged; no new tool, hardware integration or upkeep is introduced, so incremental work is zero.
unknowns: How weights are established for actual loads
research_questions: Which uncertain load or configuration facts most often delay a reliable capacity check?

already_counted.description: All weight verification and capacity checking remains.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=60+40=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. No verification time or existing indicator runtime is claimed as newly saved labour.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Guide backing trucks and secure delivery loads

steps.what: Direct truck drivers backing vehicles into loading bays while observing the actual surroundings
Cover, uncover or secure loads for delivery and inspect the actual result

tasks.design: Keep backing guidance and physical load handling with the operator. Existing site and securing guidance in {DOCS} remains a reference; no digital status is treated as proof that a bay is clear or a load is secured.
tasks.previous_blocker: Vehicle guidance and load securing require observation and physical action.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing guidance cannot perform the physical work or see current surroundings.
tasks.still_hard: Coordinate movement and respond to changing conditions and load concerns.
tasks.human_edge: See the actual surroundings and verify the physical result.
tasks.altitude: Vehicle-guidance and load-handling duties remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Maintain clear communication and check the actual load condition.

evidence.claim: Live vehicle guidance and physical load securing are not replaced by warehouse records or booking time slots.

assumptions: Boundary is operator vehicle guidance and covering or securing, excluding driving, lift operation and transport release.
The operator checks bay conditions and communicates with the driver in s1. The driver positions the vehicle in response during s1; s2 starts only after positioning, not after a stop request.
The operator inspects and handles the actual load during s2. No structured bay-clear or secured-load flag is presumed, and driver labour remains unchanged outside the focal denominator.
Native guidance access suffices; no new application, hardware or capture duty is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Site guidance duties and securing responsibilities
research_questions: Which communication failures or physical conditions most often interrupt the task?

already_counted.description: All live guidance, physical handling and inspection remains.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+55=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. Physical handling and guidance retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review schedules and special loading instructions

steps.what: Review daily work or delivery schedules to determine order, delivery sequence and special loading instructions

tasks.design: Keep review of current work and delivery instructions with the operator, using existing documents in {DOCS}. No schedule solver or generated summary substitutes for reading special loading instructions.
tasks.previous_blocker: The operator must understand the actual sequence and unusual requirements before carrying out work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing schedule access supports review, but no duplicate preparation step is established.
tasks.still_hard: Recognise conflicting instructions or changes that need planner clarification.
tasks.human_edge: Relate the documented sequence to actual equipment and site conditions.
tasks.altitude: Schedule-review duties and planning authority remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Identify conflicts and communicate uncertainties before work starts.

evidence.claim: Reviewing special loading instructions is distinct from generating schedules or reducing dock turnaround, so those capabilities do not establish review-time savings.

assumptions: Boundary is operator review and clarification, excluding planner schedule creation, dispatch and actual loading.

The planner supplies the current version of the schedule, work identifiers, sequence and special instructions through the existing planning process before s1. The operator reads them and asks about conflicts during retained s1 time; no free structured work-ready flag is assumed.
Existing planner work remains unchanged outside the focal denominator. Native document access suffices; no new system, extraction duty or upkeep is introduced, so incremental work is zero.
unknowns: Current schedule access and frequency of last-minute changes
research_questions: Which schedule changes or special instructions most often require direct clarification?

already_counted.description: All schedule reading, interpretation and clarification remains.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, gross=0, upkeep=0, net=0. No operator review time is removed and planner or dock-flow benefits are outside this boundary.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The operator retains physical coordination, load verification and instruction review; no labour reduction is claimed for these duties.
reach: Clarify site conditions and work instructions with material-moving supervisors.
skills_to_grow: Verify actual equipment and load conditions
role.ambitious_version: Maintain direct observation and clear coordination while using existing equipment information within current responsibilities.
